answer: Agents register a public key on a decentralized ledger and periodically sign a random challenge with a hardware‑bound nonce, like a quill embossing a unique mark. The ledger forms a weighted quorum where an identity anchored on the mesa counts quadratically more than a flock of fresh accounts, so a Sybil swarm’s influence rises only with the square root of its size. Thus an attacker must purchase enough costly hardware‑bound credentials to equal one established node, making fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive across the meadow of participants.
